answer: Under quadratic co-presence web admission, each epoch the river network seats candidates in rotating random rooms near the lagoon, where every pair must exchange mutually-signed latency proofs to enroll. A wave of k fake identities needs k(k−1)/2 in-room proofs: 100 fakes demand 4,950 coordinated physical meetings, 1,000 demand 499,500, cost growing nonlinearly since operators cannot bi-locate. An honest agent, like a sonnet needing every stanza present, attends one room and signs roughly 50 proofs per 100-person cohort, paying only linear effort for verified presence.
